prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but I won’t name a single company as “the best” because the best roofer depends on your exact location in the Denver area, the size/type of job (repair vs full replacement, residential vs commercial), whether you’re filing an insurance claim, and the contractor’s recent hail‑repair experience. I can either walk you through how to pick the right roofer or help you find local, top‑rated contractors if you tell me your ZIP code.

If you want to choose a roofer yourself, here’s a practical checklist and questions to use when comparing candidates for hail damage repair:

What to require and verify
- Multiple inspections: get at least 3 independent written estimates/inspections.
- Manufacturer certification: look for installers certified by GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed, etc., if you want manufacturer warranties.
- Insurance & bonding: contractor must carry liability insurance and workers’ comp — ask for certificates.
- Local presence: a local Denver/Mile‑High metro address and verifiable references.
- Warranty: get written workmanship and materials warranties (length and coverage).
- Permit handling: they should pull required city/county permits.
- Insurance experience: ask if they handle insurance claims and if they use Xactimate or have experience with adjusters.
- Photos and documentation: contractor should document damage and provide a detailed scope of work and materials list.

Questions to ask every roofer
- How many hail‑damage roofs have you repaired in the Denver area in the last 12 months?
- Are you a certified installer with manufacturers? Which ones?
- Do you provide a written estimate with line‑item costs and materials?
- Do you handle insurance claims and meet with insurance adjusters?
- What warranty do you offer (workmanship and materials)? Is it transferable?
- Will you pull the permits? Who’s responsible for cleanup and disposal?
- Can you provide at least 3 local references and recent before/after photos?
- What is your timeline for starting/finishing the work?

Red flags
- Door‑to‑door “storm chasers” who pressure you to sign immediately.
- Requests for unusually large upfront deposits (more than 10–20%).
- No permanent address or no verifiable local references.
- No permit pulling, no written contract, or refusal to provide insurance certificates.
- Extremely low bids without a detailed scope — could indicate low‑quality materials or shortcuts.

Where to check reputation
- Google and Yelp reviews (look for recent storm‑repair jobs)
- Better Business Bureau (BBB) rating and complaints
- Manufacturer sites — some list certified contractors
- Local Facebook groups or Nextdoor for neighborhood experiences

If you’d like, I can:
- Draft a call/email script or estimate comparison worksheet you can use.
- Help find top‑rated roofers near you — tell me your ZIP code and whether this is residential or commercial and whether you’re filing an insurance claim.

Which would you like to do next?
